assertions.name: A6_no_single_falloff_fits_both
assertions.source: f = +2.0301 from A-scaling vs -0.6970 from the mirror, one of them negative

description: Tests the owner's call that inter-nucleon bonds should run between ALL pairs with a falloff. The non-adjacent bond is built as the braid band generator (T5 T4 T3)(T2 + d)(T3 T4 T5)^-1, verified by its permutation to be the (2,6) swap — last strand of block 0 to first of block 2 — with no free parameter. A far bond in ISOLATION contributes exactly what an adjacent one does (ratio 1 to 1e-8), since the band is a conjugate of T_2 and the Markov trace does not see the distance: there is no intrinsic distance decay. The falloff appears only in combination, as SATURATION: with the adjacent bonds present the far bond's marginal contribution drops to 0.640829 (p-n) and 0.659916 (p-p) of its isolated value, nearly type-independent at 2.9% apart, because adjacent bonds sit at generators 3k+2 and commute while the band spans 3,4,5 and does not. This narrows the previous probe's claim: L is exactly additive over ADJACENT bonds (residual 4e-16) but not over all pairs (2e-1). Against experiment, all-pairs gives 2H/3He 0.40361 (+40.0%) and 3H/3He 1.20327 (+9.5%) against the chain's 0.50000 (+73.5%) and 1.17024 (+6.5%), so all pairs is the better topology overall — and is what atom_gen_chains already does. But no single distance weight fits both ratios (+2.03 from A-scaling, -0.70 from the mirror), refuting a one-parameter falloff.
caveats: THE OWNER'S FALLOFF IS CONFIRMED IN OUTCOME BUT NOT IN MECHANISM, and the difference is testable. A distance decay put into the bond would suppress a far bond even in isolation; saturation does not — it suppresses only the marginal contribution once neighbours are present. These predict different things at A >= 4, where a nucleon can have several far neighbours at several distances, so the two readings are separable in principle even though A = 3 cannot separate them.

NARROWS binding_lp_with_inter_nucleon_bonds_probe.py, which reported L exactly additive over bonds at 4.4e-16. That holds only over the adjacent chain, whose bonds commute. The per-bond constants L_pn, L_nn, L_pp are unaffected and still measured, but the additive law built on them does not extend to all pairs.

Only two independent ratios exist at A <= 3, so any model with two or more free falloff parameters is exactly determined by them and predicts nothing. The one-parameter version is refuted here; the per-type version is untestable without A = 4, which needs H_12 (77 partitions, Specht dimensions to 2673) and does not fit the dense seminormal route used throughout this series.
